I have been farming my 8 mu of land in Quzhou County for more than 30 years. My father taught me, and I have never seen a reason to change what works. Around here, the soil is good and flat, the irrigation wells are reliable, and the machinery services know exactly how to handle wheat and maize. I do not gamble with cotton or vegetables — prices jump around and they need too much hand labor. I will stick to the winter wheat–summer maize rotation that every household in my village follows.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. It is an improved variety, maybe Jimai 22 or Luyuan 502, the kind I buy from the seed station. I will rotary-till before sowing each year. For fertilizer, I spread compound fertilizer as a basal dose and then top-dress urea at green-up in spring. Wheat drinks more water than maize, so I irrigate four times: winter irrigation to protect against frost, then again at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I spray herbicide once and insecticide/fungicide two or three more times. I expect about 1,000 jin per mu, roughly 545 kg.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will direct-seed hybrid maize — Denghai 605 or similar — straight into the wheat stubble without tilling. No-tillage saves diesel, time, and keeps the stubble cover to hold moisture. Maize gets less irrigation, usually twice: once when it is knee-high and again at tasseling if the rains fail. I control weeds and corn borer with about four sprays in total. I expect around 1,140 jin per mu, about 570 kg.

That is my plan. It is safe, I know the costs, and the grain dealer comes to the village to buy.
